reviewer: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra Pro - AI-assisted source and execution review

decisions.basis: No new principal-authorization, token-backing or message-forgery regression was demonstrated in the reviewed delta. Retain authenticated route/asset/ISM/current-set bindings, the configured native finality policy, supported native-recipient restrictions and supervised recovery/backlog controls. Correlated RPC witnesses remain a stated trust dependency. This is not approval for arbitrary code-bearing native recipients or unlimited load.

F-06 and F-33 are now verified source closures; they are no longer the blockers. F-08 and F-19 still prevent a reliable all-chain autonomous servicing and controlled paid-obligation outcome claim. Immutable liabilities are preserved, but preservation alone is not fulfillment. This decision is based on source behavior, not missing per-host attestations.

Requires an explicitly approved operator-owned outcome/escalation process for outstanding obligations, effective restricted-role migrations, fair/backlog monitoring, exact transaction/nonce preservation and a separately authorized operating plan. No such new policy acceptance or production enablement is supplied by this audit. Never delete an uncertain obligation or re-sign it solely to recover availability.

decisions.decision: NO-GO for an unattended availability claim
decisions.basis: F-36 is a freshly reproduced application-to-worker failure-isolation defect. An admitted unprocessable item can prevent healthy queued work from progressing. Correct validation and per-item failure isolation before claiming autonomous public intake. Existing correctly deployed tokens are not invalidated, and unauthorized token ownership or minting was not demonstrated.

Only under an explicit operator-controlled intake/recovery procedure that avoids the demonstrated blocking condition and preserves every uncertain deployment identity. This does not authorize deletion of unresolved journal records. Address F-37/F-38 recovery/provenance limitations and F-39 misleading presentation.

decisions.decision: CONDITIONAL GO within the reviewed delta
decisions.basis: The known rogue-key admission cause is verified remediated on the frozen source. Fresh build/package/fork/import tests and read-only runtime/activation observations are positive. No additional Critical or High defect was demonstrated. Preserve the already activated canonical fork/manifest and normal quorum rules; do not repeat migration, restake or roll back to a pre-fix binary. This is not a whole-node audit or an attestation of every installed executable.

findings.assessment: The securityAccounting rejection, epoch-marker and parent-derived base-fee controls remain in place. The v3.5.0 executor/IBFT changes add the possession migration hook without removing these original accounting boundaries. Unchanged enforcement dependencies and the changed integration points were checked against the previous baseline.
findings.evidence: Fresh source comparison; fresh state and IBFT package execution in E-02; prior independent accounting/rejection evidence retained as inherited, not represented as a newly rerun custom suite.
findings.limits: The present fork test exercises possession migration, not every historical native exploit fixture or a Byzantine live-network proposal. RPC version strings do not establish each host binary hash.
findings.remediation: Retain the original securityAccounting configuration and regression controls. No corrective product change is required for the original resolved cause.

findings.assessment: Transaction-original storage and refund-accounting corrections remain present. State transaction/storage dependencies are unchanged; the changed executor integration was inspected for interference from the possession hook. Fresh state package tests pass.
findings.evidence: Fresh blob comparison and source review; E-02 state package result; original differential/rejection traces remain inherited evidence.
findings.limits: A passing package run is not a new exhaustive independent refund matrix. No regression of the originally resolved cause was demonstrated.
findings.remediation: Preserve original-value tracking, refund invariants and rejection tests; keep migration writes outside ordinary transaction refund semantics.

findings.assessment: The general gossip/governance admission paths still allow substantial work before complete bounded admission and deduplication. New JSON-RPC request-storage limits do not impose an equivalent global budget on every peer-originated verification path. The original availability boundary remains relevant.
findings.evidence: Fresh inspection of unchanged network/worker/governance dependencies and changed checkpoint integration; E-02/E-04 validate ordinary runtime behavior, not a full adversarial saturation campaign.
findings.limits: No production consensus outage or principal compromise was induced. This is distinct from the now-resolved unverified per-message storage cause F-32.
findings.remediation: Add cheap authenticated admission/deduplication and bounded global/per-peer work before expensive remote verification, preserving complete evidence checks before signing.

findings.assessment: Rotating bounded route retries remove the fixed-prefix starvation condition, and corrupt records no longer necessarily abort healthy siblings. Fresh repeated runtime tests support this improvement. Capacity-pressure and filesystem failure paths can still hold shared observer progress, so the finding is downgraded rather than closed.
findings.evidence: Fresh review of iln_observer_retry.go, checkpoint/storage integration and their tests; E-02 and three repeated runtime runs in E-04.
findings.limits: The narrower residual needs route-capacity pressure or persistent local I/O problems. Time-based rotation is not a proof of arbitrary-timing fairness or unlimited throughput. A durable fair-service SLA was not established.
findings.remediation: Isolate capacity/I/O failures per route, retain evidence on quarantine and measure oldest work; add capacity-saturation and restart fairness tests before claiming autonomous progress under overload.

findings.assessment: Complete source evidence is compared across distinct operator-labelled RPC witnesses, but labels and URLs do not establish independent physical upstreams. BSC and Optimism extend the same trust model. Native safe/finalized checks and fail-closed message binding remain positive controls; two correlated or colluding counted witnesses remain the relevant trust prerequisite.
findings.evidence: Fresh witness/finality/configuration source review; E-02 finality tests; E-05 live read-only observations. The unchanged quorum comparison implementation is recorded in the source matrix.
findings.limits: No false live quorum was constructed. HTTP 403/429 observations are reachability limits, not evidence of collusion or invalid chain state. Safe L2 evidence is not represented as final L1 settlement.
findings.remediation: Document actual upstream control, diversify witnesses and monitor disagreement. Reassess on correlated-provider discovery; do not weaken finality or invent new operator acceptance.

findings.assessment: The supported quote writer now receives the required narrow intent SELECT permission; the status reader receives the overtaken-obligation read dependency. Readiness checks include the new dependency. An isolated PostgreSQL test executed the real monitor queries and exact production readiness SQL under restricted roles; all required checks passed after the documented migration.
findings.evidence: E-03 restricted-roles.json/log: missing intent read detected before repair, all nine readiness checks true after repair, joined reads succeed, UPDATE/DELETE on immutable debt tables denied, unrelated role promotion rejected.
findings.limits: This verifies source/schema/role behavior in disposable PostgreSQL, not installation of the migration on every production database or a new paid quote transaction.
findings.remediation: Apply/verify the documented narrow migration during normal authorized operations and retain role-level regression tests. Do not use superuser or grant debt mutation as a workaround.

findings.assessment: Prepared exact signed transaction bytes, hash and nonce ownership remain durable before broadcast. The new Creator shared-wallet guard does not authorize replacement signing of uncertain sponsorship rows. Fresh sponsor tests preserve the original identity/recovery controls.
findings.evidence: Fresh sponsor source review and E-01 managed-relay/real-schema tests; exact-byte recovery remains separate from F-33 effect fencing.
findings.limits: No historical production orphan was resolved by this audit. Preserving a row is not proof that every old obligation has completed.
findings.remediation: Keep original transaction identity and nonce ownership through uncertainty. Investigate pre-upgrade rows under controlled reconciliation, never by blind re-signing.

findings.assessment: The repaired recovery helper bounds raced read work, but the full fresh-candidate sweep still contains serial provider-dependent preflight paths that can delay service to otherwise healthy chains. The narrower F-33 fix does not establish fair, bounded all-chain servicing.
findings.evidence: Fresh runSweep/preflight and recovery call-graph review; E-01 timeout controls pass for their actual helper scope.
findings.limits: No live outage was generated. An outer timeout around an effectful callback would reintroduce the resolved late-broadcast problem and is not an acceptable fix.
findings.remediation: Bound read-only preflight end-to-end and schedule independent chains fairly. Test a deliberately stalled provider while healthy chains progress, without cancelling or replacing uncertain sends.

findings.assessment: The native router preserves backed deferred claims and beneficiary-only withdrawal when direct native delivery fails. Mailbox completion can nevertheless still be presented as fully received principal, and arbitrary recipient contracts may lack a usable claim path. UI changes in this delta do not eliminate the original distinction.
findings.evidence: Fresh router/presentation review and E-06 native fallback tests covering reserved backing, accumulation, failed withdrawals and beneficiary authorization.
findings.limits: No unbacked claim or unauthorized withdrawal was demonstrated. The issue is recipient support and truthful completion, not a claim that every completed message loses funds.
findings.remediation: Retain the restricted code-free or separately verified claim-capable recipient policy; expose deferred native principal and the existing beneficiary-authorized recovery path explicitly.

findings.assessment: Authorized ownership/service-wallet transitions can still converge the intended independent roles. The relevant gateway ownership implementation is unchanged. This is an authorized-role separation weakness, not an arbitrary external takeover.
findings.evidence: Fresh unchanged-source comparison and ownership/fee-wallet tests within E-06.
findings.limits: The triggering actor already holds the relevant administrative authority. Ordinary token holders were not shown to gain it.
findings.remediation: Check current and pending ownership during rotation. A future contract revision should enforce role inequality across nomination, acceptance and service-wallet changes in either order.

findings.assessment: Membership signatures retain the prior deployment-unbound domain under the documented single-active-registry model. Direct transfer signatures separately bind registry/ISM identities. The existing bounded risk acceptance is retained; adding chains is not an implicit acceptance of overlapping registry migrations.
findings.evidence: Fresh Registry V3/domain review and receipt-pinned chain configuration; E-06 membership and Direct-BLS replay tests.
findings.limits: The audit did not prove absence of every unlisted alternative deployment, nor authorize simultaneous equivalent active registries. The pre-existing acceptance is not expanded.
findings.remediation: Maintain a single active receipt-pinned registry per stated domain. Reopen the design before overlapping migrations and use an explicitly versioned address-bound membership domain if the invariant changes.

findings.assessment: A minimum independently operated committee size remains an operating policy rather than a hard on-chain minimum. Correct threshold calculation does not establish independence or a minimum committee of three.
findings.evidence: Fresh registry/quorum source review and E-06 current-set membership controls.
findings.limits: Consensus migration's five proven keys must not be confused with five independent Interchain operators. Active bridge committee independence was not newly attested.
findings.remediation: Monitor the documented operating minimum and rotation continuity. Any hard minimum or altered governance rule needs a separately authorized design and migration decision.

findings.assessment: Wallet proof submission retains basic selector/target/value checks without fully decoding and binding the submitted valid message to the user's selected intent. Contract-side authorization still prevents arbitrary forged value delivery; a substituted independently valid operation remains a wallet-intent/gas-spend concern.
findings.evidence: Fresh unchanged wallet submission-path review and relevant E-01 wallet regression runs.
findings.limits: No message forgery or principal redirection through a bad signature was demonstrated. Existing proofs and source records remain required.
findings.remediation: Decode the process arguments and compare the complete authenticated message identity with the selected transfer before requesting wallet submission; test substituted valid messages.

findings.assessment: The broad isolated discovery run executes 173 test files, of which eight fail. Triage identifies stale catalog/address/copy assumptions, a configured-mail fixture dependency and a historical deployment-component alias assertion; none alone demonstrates a new principal vulnerability. Manually enumerated normal CI can still be green while these regressions fail.
findings.evidence: E-01 all 173 logs and test-failure-triage.json; E-06 is a separate 111-test Solidity result, not a substitute for the JavaScript failures.
findings.limits: Tests were not edited to obtain green results. The audit distinguishes test-file exit status from individual assertions and does not add unrelated suite totals as unique exploit counts.
findings.remediation: Update fixtures narrowly against authenticated current inventory/intentional behavior, retain negative security assertions and discover the full supported test set in CI. Preserve strict receipt/runtime validation when recognizing component aliases.

findings.assessment: Positive live contract and activation observations were obtained, but exact installed service revisions, effective production database-role migration, aged obligation outcomes and representative existing paid-operation evidence remain installation-assurance tasks. They are not fabricated source vulnerabilities.
findings.evidence: E-03 actual restricted-role test; E-05 202 endpoint observations and node runtime checks; scope-specific limitations in verification.md.
findings.limits: No new Mainnet transfer or payout was requested. BSC receipt reads were unavailable from the CI vantage point. Separate node release metadata and observed client toolchain strings differ, so per-host binary identity is not established.
findings.remediation: When a concrete installed-service approval depends on it, request existing sanitized revision/role/journal-age/outcome records and installed binary hashes. Do not turn missing evidence alone into a blanket NO-GO.

findings.assessment: Expiry release retains distinct witness comparison and canonical reread before a liability is released. The original single-view/no-reread cause remains absent. Changes elsewhere in quote lifecycle do not remove this control.
findings.evidence: Fresh source comparison/review and E-01 sponsor quote/finalized-resolution regressions; original entrypoint traces remain identified inherited evidence.
findings.limits: The audit did not perform a production expiry release. Provider physical independence remains F-05 rather than reopening the eliminated single-view implementation cause.
findings.remediation: Retain independent witness configuration, immutable liability age and canonical reread tests; monitor unresolved backlog without dropping uncertain obligations.

findings.assessment: Per-wallet request limits and durable promises bound individual admission, but unpaid payer aliases can still occupy finite aggregate sponsor capacity. The delta does not provide Sybil-resistant capacity fairness. Existing obligations remain protected rather than silently expired for availability.
findings.evidence: Fresh quote admission/commitment source review and E-01 funding/admission tests.
findings.limits: No production capacity exhaustion was attempted. A per-address limit is not an identity limit, and the audit does not invent operator acceptance of an unlimited free-admission policy.
findings.remediation: Adopt explicitly approved bounded admission and fairness controls while preserving every uncertain/paid liability. Measure saturation and recovery without adding an unrequested mandatory user signature.

findings.assessment: The conservative daily-spend plus outstanding-liability calculation can count some uncertain grants in overlapping sets. This can reject otherwise affordable new work, rather than proving treasury insolvency or duplicate payout.
findings.evidence: Fresh budget/funding arithmetic review and E-01 corresponding tests; the overlapping classification is not eliminated by the Creator's separate caps.
findings.limits: No exact production overcount amount was measured; live journals were not inspected.
findings.remediation: Define mutually exclusive confirmed-spend and unsettled-obligation categories and test real-schema transitions/windows. Preserve uncertain obligations exactly once when changing arithmetic.

findings.assessment: Paid obligations are retained when external completion overtakes service, but recording an overtaken state is not a complete controlled-outcome process. Stopping new admission and servicing old debt are still insufficiently separated. This remains a blocker for an unrestricted unattended servicing claim even after F-33 is fixed.
findings.evidence: Fresh lifecycle, global-disable, overtaken-record and monitor review; E-01/E-03 establish durability and restricted reads, not fulfillment of every promise.
findings.limits: A staffed, explicitly approved outcome/escalation process may support a narrower operation. No such new policy was accepted on the operator's behalf. Automatic late gifts or debt deletion are not recommended.
findings.remediation: Separate stop-new-admission from safe old-obligation reconciliation and implement operator-owned traceable outcomes with escalation. Preserve original nonce, transaction identity and liabilities throughout uncertainty.

findings.assessment: Missing-route and undelivered-vote retention are improved, and ordinary expired-set handoff tests pass. A narrower source path remains in which a success return does not uniformly prove durable successor persistence before the original locator is removed. Therefore the original consume-before-success cause is not fully closed.
findings.evidence: Fresh caller/callee source proof across checkpoint, direct signing and durable storage; E-02/E-04 positive retention/handoff regressions. No new full end-to-end negative execution for this narrower branch is claimed.
findings.limits: This is a refinement of the existing finding, not a new duplicate finding. Public material omits a runnable unresolved trigger sequence. Known-hash recovery can mitigate availability but does not prove atomic handoff.
findings.remediation: Make persistence/terminal-delivery status explicit, not inferred from a generic nil error. Delete original evidence only after authenticated completion or an atomic verified durable successor; test ineligible/failed persistence and restart cases.

findings.assessment: A syntactically successful but incomplete discovery response can still advance a durable scan cursor. Full two-witness authorization of each discovered message does not itself prove completeness of the discovery list.
findings.evidence: Fresh scan/observer source review and unchanged-dependency comparison; E-02 ordinary discovery tests.
findings.limits: No unauthorized mint is implied: missing messages affect availability and discovery. No false live response was injected into production.
findings.remediation: Use bounded overlapping reconciliation or independently checked completeness, retain known-hash recovery and alert on differing windows. Never weaken complete source verification to gain progress.

findings.assessment: BSC admin reconciliation now recognizes finalized evidence and checks the canonical receipt block. The corresponding admin branch does not uniformly apply the safe policy requested for the L2 configurations, where confirmation-depth promotion remains. The Direct-BLS runtime's safe verification is a separate, stronger path.
findings.evidence: Fresh admin deployment-finality and BSC/OP configuration review; E-01 chain-finality tests and E-02 runtime finality tests; E-05 deployment observations.
findings.limits: No presently deployed contract mismatch or invalid validator signature was demonstrated. Read-only receipt identity checks are not a proof that every admin status path uses native finality.
findings.remediation: Share the chain-native safe/finalized policy across admin reconciliation, pin receipt height/hash and canonical rereads, and keep provisional depth labels distinct from final approval.

findings.assessment: Exclusive deployment-intent locks can still survive an owner crash without a safe automatic owner/lease recovery protocol. Related operator locks require conservative recovery; age alone cannot prove that no transaction is in flight.
findings.evidence: Fresh admin intent/journal/locking source review and E-01 deployment recovery tests.
findings.limits: No lock was deleted or service restarted. This is bounded operational availability, not authority to discard an uncertain deployment or duplicate a nonce.
findings.remediation: Provide explicit stale-owner verification and journal-preserving recovery. Preserve exact signed bytes, nonce and hash; never delete a lock solely because it is old.

findings.assessment: The paid-fee backfill still constructs an event without the complete message/source-transaction identity required by verified storage. Error handling can hold progress instead of producing the intended independently bound record. The unrelated indexed open-count change does not repair this path.
findings.evidence: Fresh backfillPaidFeeTax/storeVerifiedOperation call-site review and source comparison.
findings.limits: No fabricated verified record or stolen fee was demonstrated. The present audit does not claim a new actual-database backfill reproduction.
findings.remediation: Pass the verified row's message ID and source transaction hash into the stored event and add a successful-store regression with real schema constraints.

findings.assessment: Dense event windows still lack complete adaptive splitting/progress in the affected indexer path. Retrying the same overfull range can hold the cursor. Node-side bounded scans elsewhere do not close this distinct indexer cause.
findings.evidence: Fresh indexer window/cursor review and E-01 worker tests; unchanged relevant dependency paths recorded.
findings.limits: No dense Mainnet load was generated. The safety-preserving held cursor is preferable to silently skipping logs, but remains an availability limit.
findings.remediation: Split bounded ranges adaptively and define a safe dense-single-block strategy. Advance only after complete canonical processing, retaining uncertainty rather than dropping records.

findings.assessment: The corrected exact active source/route-pair selection precedes the batch limit, preventing unrelated unknown-route rows from occupying all selected work. The original query-level starvation cause remains removed.
findings.evidence: Fresh source comparison and E-01 exact-pair fairness regression; prior actual PostgreSQL negative/positive evidence remains inherited where not newly repeated.
findings.limits: Other provider waits and dense-window limits remain separately tracked. This closure is not an unlimited throughput guarantee.
findings.remediation: Retain exact-pair filtering before LIMIT and the unrelated-row starvation regression.

findings.assessment: Versioned build/linker identity controls remain corrected, and both observed XGR endpoints expose nonempty v3.5.0 client strings. The new release workflows preserve explicit revision/version checks.
findings.evidence: Fresh source/workflow review, E-02 build and E-05 client responses; canonical activation documentation is contextual evidence.
findings.limits: A nonempty version string is not a binary checksum. The observed Go toolchain string differs from the documented published asset toolchain; that traceability gap is explicitly retained in the companion review, without reopening the old empty-field cause.
findings.remediation: Maintain nonempty version/commit checks and compare actual installed executable hashes with the intended release in ordinary operations.

findings.assessment: The XITA compiler remains the recorded optimized via-IR Solidity 0.8.24 build. Fresh compilation/runtime provenance checks are positive, but they do not establish semantic equivalence or close a project-specific compiler applicability question. No historical unverified advisory identifier is adopted as a verified fact.
findings.evidence: Frozen foundry settings, E-06 build/import/constructor checks and E-05 runtime identity observations.
findings.limits: No project miscompilation, affected official advisory trigger or principal-loss path was demonstrated. Node staking's separately pinned Solidity 0.8.30 is a different artifact set.
findings.remediation: Keep this an assurance task. Qualify a specific official issue and exact trigger/settings before asserting exposure; use targeted equivalence or corrected-build evidence rather than ordering redeployment from an unverified historical claim.

findings.assessment: Membership/governance transaction submission retains unbounded remote wait paths outside the repaired sponsor helper. A slow external provider can prevent complete worker shutdown/progress. The possession migration does not repair these unchanged submission dependencies.
findings.evidence: Fresh worker/txrelayer/client call-graph inspection and exact-source comparison.
findings.limits: No forced production provider outage or node shutdown was performed. An outer timer alone cannot safely roll back a send whose outcome is unknown.
findings.remediation: Carry bounded contexts through preflight, submission and receipt waits; test complete Worker.Close termination while preserving original transaction and nonce identity for uncertain sends.

findings.assessment: Delayed-grant monitoring continues to use immutable creation age rather than mutable retry/heartbeat timestamps. The required status-reader privilege is now also repaired under F-06.
findings.evidence: Fresh source review, E-01 age regressions and E-03 actual restricted monitor query execution.
findings.limits: Actual production alert delivery and aged journal contents were not inspected. Those operational checks do not reopen the resolved age-predicate defect.
findings.remediation: Retain immutable-age predicates and validate installed alert delivery using existing sanitized/synthetic monitoring evidence.

findings.assessment: An explicit destination receipt failure can still coexist with a retained submitted/pending stage and misleading waiting wording. The delta's transfer-selection and copy changes do not consistently give the failure state precedence.
findings.evidence: Fresh transfer status/flow source review and E-01 existing presentation tests; no new wallet transaction was submitted.
findings.limits: The original source evidence should remain valid; a failed destination execution is not a reason to repeat the source lock. This is presentation/recovery guidance rather than message authorization.
findings.remediation: Prioritize authenticated destination failure and offer only the appropriate destination retry while preserving source transaction/message identity.

findings.assessment: Unverified unknown-route request directories now have global admission/retention bounds and expiry cleanup. Verified votes and unfinished authenticated recovery evidence are not swept under the unverified-hint policy. The original permanent unbounded request-storage cause is removed.
findings.evidence: Fresh JSON-RPC/storage policy review; E-02 package tests and E-04 three repeated JSON-RPC/runtime runs including bound/expiry/churn controls.
findings.limits: This is not a general guarantee against every local disk exhaustion or expensive peer workload. Those broader resource boundaries remain F-03/F-04.
findings.remediation: Retain bounded unverified admission and age-based cleanup tests, including restart behavior and preservation of authenticated work.

findings.assessment: The raced recovery inspector now returns read-only observations/action descriptors. Only the still-active caller may pass bounded rechecks and broadcast the original signed bytes. The controlled slow-read regression verifies that resolving an old timed-out read cannot newly start the payout effect.
findings.evidence: Fresh source call-graph review and E-01 effect-boundary/timeout tests. Exact-byte and uncertain-send ownership remain enforced.
findings.limits: Cancellation is not rollback of a broadcast already started, and a last-read-to-mining race is not claimed eliminated. The closure addresses the original asynchronous callback that initiated a new effect after timeout.
findings.remediation: Preserve the read/effect separation and negative late-resolution tests; keep uncertain sends durable. Do not wrap effectful callbacks in a timeout race as an apparent simplification.

findings.assessment: Recovered inclusion and provisional spendable projection are still not uniformly synchronized with durable submitted identity and later canonical evidence. A reserved row can retain incomplete transaction projection, and a provisional marker can outlive disproven inclusion.
findings.evidence: Fresh sponsor recovery/projection source review; E-01 relevant tests are positive controls but do not establish closure of the remaining branches.
findings.limits: Provisional spendability is distinct from final settlement. No duplicate payout or principal loss is asserted merely from a stale projection.
findings.remediation: Persist recovered transaction identity/submitted transition atomically, and downgrade disproven provisional inclusion without deleting the underlying obligation or reassigning its nonce.

findings.assessment: The onward optional gas observer now skips the addressed out-of-scope case, but the delivery observer can still hold an entire range on missing/unmatched optional data. A fix to one sampling cursor does not close both paths.
findings.evidence: Fresh comparison of onward and delivery observer control flow; E-01 gas observer tests cover their stated path only.
findings.limits: This is optional statistical sampling, separate from authenticated main transfer/debt cursors. No authorization weakening is recommended to obtain metric progress.
findings.remediation: Give both optional observers bounded independent progress while retaining accepted-sample verification. Test missing profiles/unmatched operations without advancing mandatory financial cursors unsafely.

findings.title: Creator queue lacks per-item failure isolation
findings.cause: An admitted, email-confirmed request can remain unprocessable by the deployment worker while occupying the first work position.
findings.assessment: An independent isolated reproduction accepted and confirmed a request, then observed three blocked worker sweeps with no healthy sibling progress. A controlled positive fixture demonstrated that otherwise valid work can progress. Two validation-boundary variants share this same missing isolation cause and are counted once.
findings.evidence: E-07 protected Creator reproduction/result hashes; real registration and worker code with mocked RPC/mail effects. Zero real broadcasts.
findings.limits: No unauthorized token ownership, minting or principal theft was demonstrated. Detailed unresolved input recipes and executable fixtures are withheld from public publication. Test-fixture removal is not a production recovery instruction.
findings.remediation: Reject unprocessable configurations before admission, isolate each item's bounded failure/backoff/quarantine and continue healthy work. Preserve all uncertain signed deployment identities and add negative/positive queue-progress tests.

findings.title: Contact retention can remove unresolved Creator deployment evidence
findings.cause: Financial recovery identity shares a deletion lifecycle with an expiring private contact record.
findings.assessment: A clock-controlled isolated test observed an unresolved deployment-submitted record, including signed recovery identity, removed when the configured long contact-retention period expired. Durable nonce/transaction recovery should not depend on retaining personal contact data indefinitely.
findings.evidence: E-07 protected Creator retention reproduction and source review of private storage/operator recovery.
findings.limits: The default long retention period is a material prerequisite. No real production record was removed, and no duplicate send or nonce reuse was demonstrated.
findings.remediation: Separate contact/PII retention from immutable unresolved deployment evidence. Purge recovery state only after authenticated terminal completion and retain minimal nonpersonal identity until then.

findings.title: Creator child-token proof comparison omits canonical block identity
findings.cause: The proof projection compared between witnesses does not retain all receipt block-identity information used by the underlying observations.
findings.assessment: An independent injected-RPC test accepted two differing receipt block identities after they collapsed to the same child-token proof projection. Token address/owner/supply checks remain; the defect is narrower canonical provenance, not demonstrated token forgery. The separate factory deployment verifier has stronger block binding.
findings.evidence: E-07 protected witness-projection reproduction; fresh child-token versus factory verification source comparison.
findings.limits: No fabricated token or unauthorized owner was demonstrated. Two endpoints are still not a cryptographic light client or proof of infrastructure independence.
findings.remediation: Compare chain, block height and block hash in the verified child proof and require canonical numbered-block rereads before promotion. Retain all token feature/runtime checks.

findings.title: Mintable Creator presentation retains a no-additional-minting label
findings.cause: A constant user-facing label is not derived from the selected validated token feature configuration.
findings.assessment: A fresh rendering assertion shows the no-additional-minting label for a mintable token while the advanced fields also disclose mint permissions and the cap. The result is contradictory presentation, not an authorization bypass.
findings.evidence: E-07 protected presentation assertion/result hashes and current Creator UI source.
findings.limits: Owner/minter controls and lifetime cap tests pass. No unauthorized mint was demonstrated.
findings.remediation: Derive the summary label from the validated token type and render every fixed/burnable/mintable variant in regression tests.

failure_triage.explanation: Two assertions retain an earlier Base XGR token address rather than the current authenticated catalog representation.
Assertions assume two routes and no route-free Creator profile; the frozen product contains the expanded route inventory and verified XITACAN profile.
The assertion expects the previous continuation label; the current status/continuation wording changed.
An earlier Base representation address remains hard-coded in the fixture.

failure_triage.classification: Stale inventory and fail-closed projection assumptions
failure_triage.explanation: The fixture assumes one asset/read where the current catalog supplies additional assets; removing a required representation now removes the unverified route rather than manufacturing the expected unavailable row.
The negative fixture rejects a numbered-block eth_call that the documented pinned-read policy intentionally permits. Forbidden write-method rejection remains required.

The injected delivery stub bypasses one outer check but the inner registration handler still requires configured transport; the isolated unconfigured fixture returns 503. A configured production failure is not established.

The old gate expects a requiredHook component name where current receipt bindings use the authenticated dispatchHook alias with the same address/runtime identity. Correct alias validation narrowly; do not bypass deployment checks.
